name: Bench Press
description: Horizontal pressing movement for chest strength.
instructions: Lie flat with eyes under the bar, feet planted, shoulder blades pinched.
Unrack and lower the bar to mid-chest with elbows about 45-60° from your torso.
Press up and slightly back until arms are straight.
Rack the bar only when the set is finished.
safety: Use a spotter or safety arms for heavy sets.
Keep wrists stacked over elbows and do not bounce the bar.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
description: Angled press emphasizing the upper chest.
instructions: Set the bench to 30-45° and sit back with dumbbells at chest level.
Press the weights up until arms are straight above the upper chest.
Lower slowly until you feel a stretch across the chest.
safety: Do not flare elbows to 90°.
Kick the dumbbells up from the knees instead of jerking them.

name: Push-up
description: Bodyweight horizontal push; use an elevated surface to scale difficulty.
instructions: Place hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower your chest to just above the floor.
Push the floor away until arms are straight.
safety: Keep hips from sagging.
Elevate your hands on a bench to make it easier.

name: Cable Chest Fly
description: Horizontal shoulder adduction with controlled range.
instructions: Stand in the middle of two cable stations with a slight forward lean.
With soft elbows, bring the handles together in front of the chest.
Return slowly until you feel a chest stretch.
safety: Keep a constant slight elbow bend.
Use a weight you can control through the whole range.

name: Lat Pulldown
description: Vertical pulling movement for the lats.
instructions: Sit with thighs secured and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulders.
Lean back slightly and pull the bar to the upper chest.
Control the bar back up until arms are straight.
safety: Do not pull the bar behind your neck.
Avoid swinging the torso to move the weight.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: Horizontal pull emphasizing mid-back musculature.
instructions: Sit tall with knees slightly bent and arms extended.
Pull the handle to your lower ribs, squeezing shoulder blades together.
Return slowly without rounding the back.
safety: Keep the chest up and spine neutral.
Do not use momentum from the lower back.

name: Pull-up
description: Vertical bodyweight pull; use assistance if needed.
reps: As many quality reps as possible
instructions: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip, shoulders away from your ears.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving the elbows down.
Lower under control to a full hang.
safety: Use a band or assisted machine if you cannot do full reps.
Avoid kipping while learning.

name: Barbell Bicep Curl
description: Elbow flexion exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Stand tall with an underhand shoulder-width grip.
Curl the bar up while keeping elbows beside your ribs.
Lower slowly to full arm extension.
safety: Do not swing your back.
Choose a load that lets you keep strict form.

name: Hammer Curl
description: Neutral-grip curl that trains elbow flexors and forearms.
instructions: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other.
Curl one or both dumbbells up without rotating the wrists.
Lower with control.
safety: Keep elbows still.
Avoid shrugging the shoulders.

name: Triceps Pushdown
description: Elbow extension with upper arms kept stable.
instructions: Stand facing a high cable, elbows pinned to your sides.
Push the handle down until arms are fully extended.
Let it rise until forearms are just past 90°.
safety: Do not let elbows drift forward.
Keep the torso upright.

name: Overhead Shoulder Press
description: Overhead press for shoulder and triceps strength.
instructions: Stand or sit with dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press overhead until arms are extended without leaning back.
Lower to shoulder height under control.
safety: Brace your core to avoid arching.
Stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder.

name: Lateral Raise
description: Shoulder abduction with light, controlled resistance.
instructions: Stand holding light dumbbells at your sides.
Raise arms out to the sides to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend.
Lower slowly.
safety: Use light weights; do not swing.
Do not raise above shoulder height.

name: Back Squat
description: Compound squat; learn technique with light loads first.
instructions: Set the bar on your upper back, feet shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Sit down and back until thighs are at least parallel.
Drive through mid-foot to stand.
safety: Learn with light loads or a goblet squat first.
Use safety pins in a rack.

name: Goblet Squat
description: Front-loaded squat variation useful for learning squat mechanics.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest.
Squat down between your knees keeping the chest tall.
Stand up by pushing through the whole foot.
safety: Keep heels flat.
Do not let knees collapse inward.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: Hip hinge emphasizing hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Stand holding the weight at your thighs, knees soft.
Push your hips back, sliding the weight down your legs.
Stop at a hamstring stretch, then drive hips forward to stand.
safety: Keep your back flat throughout.
Keep the weight close to your legs.

name: Plank
description: Isometric trunk stabilization exercise.
instructions: Place forearms on the floor with elbows under shoulders.
Form a straight line from head to heels.
Hold, breathing steadily.
safety: Do not let your lower back sag.
Stop when form breaks down.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: Flat press with a deeper stretch than the barbell version.
instructions: Lie back with dumbbells at chest level.
Press up until arms are straight over the chest.
Lower with control to a comfortable stretch.
safety: Do not let the dumbbells drift wide.
Ask for a hand-off when lifting heavy dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Fly
description: Isolation movement for the chest using a wide arc.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding dumbbells above your chest, elbows soft.
Open the arms in a wide arc until you feel a stretch.
Squeeze the chest to bring the weights back together.
safety: Use light weights.
Stop the stretch before the shoulders feel strained.

name: Bent-over Barbell Row
description: Horizontal pull for overall back thickness.
instructions: Hinge forward with a flat back and the bar below the knees.
Row the bar to your lower ribs, elbows close to the body.
Lower under control without standing up.
safety: Keep the spine neutral.
Reduce the load if your hips rise first.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
description: Single-arm row supported on a bench.
instructions: Place one hand and knee on a bench, back flat.
Row the dumbbell to your hip.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
safety: Do not twist the torso.
Keep the neck neutral.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
description: Simple shoulder elevation for the upper traps.
instructions: Stand holding heavy dumbbells at your sides.
Lift shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause, then lower slowly.
safety: Do not roll the shoulders.
Keep your neck relaxed.

name: Back Extension
description: Controlled spinal extension on a back-extension bench.
instructions: Set the pad at hip level and cross arms on chest.
Lower the torso with a straight back.
Raise until your body forms a straight line.
safety: Do not hyper-extend at the top.
Move slowly.

name: Deadlift
description: Full-body hip hinge lifting a barbell from the floor.
instructions: Stand with the bar over mid-foot and grip just outside the legs.
Brace, push the floor away and stand tall.
Lower by pushing the hips back, keeping the bar close.
safety: Learn the pattern with light weight first.
Never round the lower back.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: Seated press that trains all three deltoid heads.
instructions: Sit with back support and dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press upward until arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly to ear level.
safety: Do not arch the lower back.
Keep wrists straight.

name: Rear Delt Fly
description: Bent-over raise for the rear shoulder.
instructions: Hinge forward with a flat back, dumbbells hanging.
Raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
safety: Use light weights.
Keep the neck in line with your spine.

name: Arnold Press
description: Rotating press that works the shoulder through a longer range.
instructions: Start with palms facing you at chest height.
Rotate the palms forward as you press overhead.
Reverse the rotation as you lower.
safety: Use a lighter load than a standard press.
Avoid leaning back.

name: Face Pulls
description: Rope pull toward the face for rear shoulders and upper back.
instructions: Set a rope on a cable at head height.
Pull the rope toward your face, elbows high and wide.
Return with control.
safety: Keep the load light.
Do not lean back to move the weight.

name: Front Raises
description: Raise weights forward to shoulder height.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Raise one or both arms forward to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
safety: Do not swing.
Stop at shoulder height.

name: Upright Row
description: Vertical pull to the lower chest.
instructions: Hold the weight in front of your thighs.
Lift it to chest height, elbows leading.
Lower under control.
safety: Stop at chest height to protect the shoulders.
Use a slightly wider grip.

name: Overhead Triceps Extension
description: Overhead elbow extension that stretches the long head.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Bend the elbows to lower it behind your head.
Extend until arms are straight.
safety: Keep elbows pointing forward.
Do not arch the lower back.

name: Reverse Barbell Curl
description: Overhand-grip curl focusing on the forearms.
instructions: Hold the bar with an overhand grip.
Curl up keeping wrists straight.
Lower slowly.
safety: Use less weight than a regular curl.
Do not bend the wrists.

name: Farmer's Carry
description: Walk with heavy weights to build grip and posture.
instructions: Pick up heavy dumbbells and stand tall.
Walk with short controlled steps.
Set the weights down carefully.
safety: Keep shoulders back and down.
Choose a clear walking path.

name: Walking Lunge
description: Alternating forward lunges.
instructions: Step forward and lower until both knees are about 90°.
Push through the front foot and step into the next lunge.
Keep the torso upright.
safety: Keep the front knee over the middle of the foot.
Hold a wall for balance if needed.

name: Hip Thrust
description: Bridge with the upper back on a bench to load the glutes.
instructions: Rest your upper back on a bench with the weight on your hips.
Drive the hips up until the body is in a straight line.
Lower slowly.
safety: Tuck the chin and keep ribs down.
Use a pad on the hips.

name: Glute Bridge
description: Floor bridge for glute activation.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Push through your heels to lift the hips.
Squeeze the glutes at the top and lower.
safety: Avoid over-arching the lower back.
Keep the knees pointing forward.

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: Rise onto the toes to train the calves.
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or floor.
Rise as high as possible onto your toes.
Lower to a full stretch.
safety: Hold a wall for balance.
Move slowly without bouncing.

name: Crunch
description: Short-range trunk flexion on the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Curl your shoulders off the floor.
Lower with control.
safety: Do not pull on your neck.
Exhale as you curl up.

name: Lying Leg Raise
description: Raise straight legs to train the lower abs.
instructions: Lie flat with hands under your hips.
Raise legs until vertical.
Lower slowly without arching your back.
safety: Bend the knees if the lower back lifts.
Move slowly.

name: Russian Twist
description: Seated rotation to train the obliques.
instructions: Sit leaning back slightly with knees bent.
Rotate your torso side to side.
Keep the chest tall.
safety: Keep the spine long.
Lower the feet to the floor to make it easier.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: Lateral flexion with a dumbbell in one hand.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell at your side.
Bend sideways toward the weight.
Return to upright using your obliques.
safety: Do not twist.
Use a moderate weight.
